MEASURED 2026-08-20, answering Anthony's question about why modularization matters for the flo2 relationship: *"if we modularize, we can start following interfaces between where module-X of reflow2 interfaces with module-A from flo2. Then say flo2 requires some new feature, that requires module-X to change. This in turn could cause module-X to impose changes on module-Y... in some chain like effect."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE CHAIN CANNOT BE FOLLOWED, AND THE REASON IS NOT MISSING EDGES

Walking ONLY the coupling edges a change would actually travel — PROVIDES, CONSUMES, DEPENDS_ON, with CONTAINS deliberately excluded because containment is "part of" and not "affected by":

  ifc:core-api             reaches 36 of 56 components
  ifc:mcp-tools            reaches 36 of 56 components
  ifc:graph-export         reaches 36 of 56 components
  ifc:req-dyno-graph-api   reaches 36 of 56 components

**EVERY BOUNDARY REACHES THE SAME 36.** Component clusters: [36, 1, 1], plus **18 components with NO coupling edge of any kind**.

⇒ So "which modules must change?" has exactly two possible answers today: **36, or 0.** Never a chain. Anthony's worry that it "would be somewhat challenging to say where something may need to change" is confirmed, and it is not challenging — it is not answerable.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE INSIGHT THAT REFRAMES THE WORK: MODULARIZATION IS NOT ABOUT ADDING EDGES. IT IS ABOUT ADDING WALLS.

The 36 are one connected blob because the coupling that exists is undifferentiated DEPENDS_ON with **nothing for propagation to stop at**. Adding more edges makes the blob bigger. What makes a chain followable is BOUNDARIES that a blast radius terminates on — which is exactly what `cap:key-interfaces` was built for: *"designate a published boundary, and compute whether a change stays behind it."*

Severability IS "the blast radius stops at the boundary" (`req:modularity-computed`). With 42 of 56 components carrying no interface at all and 73 uncontracted dependency pairs, there are no walls, so the whole design is one room and severability is not a computation anyone can run.

📌 CORROBORATED FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION, same measurement: `propagate_from(ifc:core-api)` over ALL edge types returns **1,145 impacted nodes — 43% of the design**. The direct ring is 3. So the two available answers are "3 nodes" or "half the graph", because past the first hop the walk leaves the structural chain entirely and travels the GOVERNANCE web (877 of 901 GOVERNED_BY edges land on Decisions). Structural chain and reasoning web are conflated, and only the first one answers "what else must change?".

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT THIS MAKES CONCRETE ABOUT THE FLO2 CASE

`dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` already settled the TRANSPORT half — a customer levying a requirement on a supplier is ordinary SE, the schema expresses it today (`source`, `provenance: imported`, `status: proposed`, AUTHORED_BY), and plain git carries it. That node closes with the prerequisite: *"reflow2 declares NO `required` interface at all, so nothing pairs across any seam — the channel this node is about has no labelled boundary to run along."*

⚠️ THAT LINE IS NOW PARTLY STALE and should not be quoted as current: reflow2 has **9 `required` and 4 `published`** interfaces as of 2026-08-20. The boundary a flo2 requirement would LAND on now exists. What still does not exist is anything for the consequence to TRAVEL along once it has landed.

⇒ SO THE FOUR STEPS OF ANTHONY'S SCENARIO SPLIT CLEANLY:
  1. flo2 levies a requirement            — transport solved, zero new code
  2. it lands on a reflow2 boundary       — possible now (13 designated interfaces)
  3. trace it to the module that must change — possible (138 ALLOCATED_TO edges)
  4. **what that change imposes on the next module** — **NOT POSSIBLE.** Step 4 is the chain effect, and it is the whole of what modularization would buy.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether flo2's own graph has boundaries on its side. The seam is two-ended and only reflow2's end was measured here.
